main_body: Stone well basin under a snow-covered roof: a rim with a dark water opening, and a banded stone front below
top_band: Light grey stone rim, rows ~15-16, around the dark opening ellipse (rows 17-22). The snow roof above also shows a light top band at rows 1-7.
evidence: In the middle column the grey rim comes first. Below it is a dark teal-black ellipse with a brown lid or bucket, which reads as a recessed opening seen from above. A lighter front rim line follows at about row 22-23, then the stone front (rows 23-30) with dark horizontal courses. The snow roof is a wide foreshortened top band over the posts. The opening is visible and the front face sits below it, so it passes as 3/4.

style.evidence: The snow roof is decent, with blue-white steps and icicles. The stone base is thinner than the reference well: flat grey blocks with plain dark stripes, no stone-by-stone shading, and large uniform fills in the opening and the posts. Outlines lean dark brown or blue, not pure black. Overall it is a bit flatter and sparser than the roofed-well reference.
